about: Byte vectors authored by Apache Kafka's own MemoryRecordsBuilder, the class its producer uses to lay out a batch. Regenerate with `cargo xtask records --refresh`; never edit a hex by hand.

vectors.name: one_record_no_key
vectors.why: The smallest batch: one record, no key, no headers, no compression, every optional batch field at its Kafka sentinel. Everything else here is a departure from this.

vectors.name: one_record_with_key
vectors.why: A key present alongside the value. Key and value are both zigzag-varint length-prefixed and a null key is -1 rather than 0, so absent and empty must stay distinct.

vectors.name: an_empty_key_and_an_empty_value
vectors.why: Empty is not absent. A zero-length key encodes as varint 0 where a null key encodes as -1, and the pair is the one distinction a length alone cannot carry.

vectors.name: a_null_value
vectors.why: A tombstone. Kafka writes a null value as varint -1, which is what makes a delete distinguishable from an empty payload.

vectors.name: three_records_with_deltas
vectors.why: Offset and timestamp deltas are per-record and relative to the batch, so a batch of one can never show whether the base is being subtracted. maxTimestamp must land on the largest, not the last.

vectors.name: headers_on_one_record
vectors.why: Record headers are a varint count then key/value pairs, the header key being a plain length-prefixed string and its value nullable. Nothing else in the batch reaches this framing.

vectors.name: transactional_with_producer_identity
vectors.why: The producer fields and the transactional attribute bit travel in the batch header, not in any record. This is the only case that puts a non-sentinel value in producerId, producerEpoch, baseSequence, and partitionLeaderEpoch at once.

vectors.name: log_append_time
vectors.why: The timestamp-type attribute is bit 3. Under LogAppendTime Kafka stamps the batch rather than the record, so the bit and the timestamps must be read together.

vectors.name: a_large_batch_needing_multibyte_varints
vectors.why: Every length in a record is a zigzag varint, so a payload past 63 bytes is the first that needs two continuation bytes. A corpus of short records would never exercise the multi-byte path at all.

vectors.name: compression_twin_uncompressed
vectors.why: The same two records as the four compressed batches, stored verbatim. It is the control: decompressing any codec must produce exactly these records, which is the half of compression that CAN be held to Kafka's bytes.

vectors.name: gzip
vectors.why: Compression replaces the records payload wholesale and sets attribute bits 0-2. The batch header stays uncompressed, which is what lets a broker read a batch it cannot decompress.

vectors.name: snappy
vectors.why: Kafka's snappy is the xerial FRAMED format, whose payload opens with a 0x82 'SNAPPY' magic, not the raw snappy an implementation reaching for the obvious crate would produce.

vectors.name: lz4
vectors.why: LZ4 here is the frame format, opening with the 0x04224D18 frame magic rather than a bare block.

vectors.name: zstd
vectors.why: Zstd's frame magic is 0x28B52FFD. Included for the same reason as its siblings: the codec identity lives in the attributes, and reading the wrong one produces a plausible-looking failure deep inside the payload.
